security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU emulates Smidctrl/Ssidctrl but fails to remove the WARL-forced eidelivery=0x20000000 behavior and continues to expose eithreshold as subsuming APLIC ithreshold. Guest software built against the updated spec expects eidelivery and eithreshold to be outside Smidctrl scope (i.e., behave per base AIA or be absent), and instead finds eidelivery hardwired to ACLIC-only mode with eithreshold aliasing APLIC state, breaking the guest's interrupt delivery model.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: smuidctrl OR ssidctrl flag check that gates eidelivery WARL 0x20000000 or eithreshold-to-ithreshold aliasing; any CSR read/write handler for eidelivery/eithreshold that branches on smstateen/mstateen Smidctrl/Ssidctrl bits; missing mithreshold CSR when Smidctrl/Ssidctrl is enabled
security_spec.summary: Stale eidelivery/eithreshold emulation after spec removes them from Smidctrl/Ssidctrl scope blocks or corrupts guest interrupt delivery when guest targets the updated spec

findings.finding: The AIA indirect CSR dispatch (rmw_xireg_aia) correctly routes IMSIC ISELECT values (ISELECT_IMSIC_EIDELIVERY, ISELECT_IMSIC_EITHRESHOLD) to the imsic->rmw_fn callback without any Smidctrl/Ssidctrl WARL gating logic. No smstateen branch on Smidctrl/Ssidctrl bits exists. The dispatch checks ext_smaia/ext_ssaia flags only. Compliant because Smidctrl/Ssidctrl are not implemented at all, so there are no incorrect WARL overrides.

IMSIC eidelivery WARL mask is correctly constrained to bit 0 only (wr_mask &= 0x1). No 0x20000000 hardwiring. No Smidctrl/Ssidctrl gating. The write triggers riscv_imsic_update() for correct side-effect (interrupt delivery re-evaluation).

IMSIC eithreshold WARL mask uses IMSIC_MAX_ID (0x7ff), correctly constraining the threshold to valid interrupt ID range. No aliasing to APLIC ithreshold. No Smidctrl/Ssidctrl gating. Write triggers riscv_imsic_update() for correct side-effect.

IMSIC page selection logic correctly isolates M-mode vs S-mode IMSIC devices (if imsic->mmode, only priv==PRV_M accesses page 0; otherwise only priv==PRV_S). M-mode and S-mode IMSICs are separate device instances in virt machine, so eithreshold[0] in the M-mode IMSIC and eithreshold[0] in the S-mode IMSIC do not alias. Compliant — no unauthorized cross-privilege threshold sharing.

The miselect/mireg CSR predicate checks only ext_smaia and ext_smcsrind flags. There are no Smidctrl/Ssidctrl bits defined in the mstateen wr_mask. No vulnerability pattern exists because the feature is absent.

mstateen0 WR mask includes SMSTATEEN0_AIA (bit 59) and SMSTATEEN0_IMSIC (bit 58) only when ext_smaia is enabled. No Smidctrl or Ssidctrl bits are defined or writable. The vulnerability pattern (smuidctrl/ssidctrl flag check gating eidelivery/eithreshold WARL) cannot manifest without the bits existing.
IMSIC VMState correctly serializes eidelivery, eithreshold, and eistate arrays for live migration. Arrays are sized by num_pages. No missing fields. Migration correctness is maintained.
findings.snippet:
VMSTATE_VARRAY_UINT32(eidelivery, RISCVIMSICState, num_pages, 0, ...)
VMSTATE_VARRAY_UINT32(eithreshold, RISCVIMSICState, num_pages, 0, ...)

findings.finding: eidelivery and eithreshold arrays are initialized via g_new0 (all-zero) during realize(), and allocation is skipped under KVM (kvm_irqchip_in_kernel). Reset values are correct: delivery disabled, threshold 0 (no masking). No explicit cpu_reset path needed because IMSIC is a device, not CPU state.
findings.snippet:
imsic->eidelivery = g_new0(uint32_t, imsic->num_pages);
imsic->eithreshold = g_new0(uint32_t, imsic->num_pages);

findings.finding: APLIC idelivery and ithreshold are independent MMIO-accessed per-hart registers with correct WARL (idelivery: bit 0; ithreshold: iprio_mask). No aliasing with IMSIC eithreshold/eidelivery. The APLIC and IMSIC threshold/delivery registers are in separate device instances with separate memory regions. No cross-device aliasing exists.
